messages:
maria: Quick heads-up — saw a ~15-18% p99 latency regression on fp8 paths for seq_len=512 when continuous batching is enabled. Repro harness attached and profiler shows lots of padding-related kernels being picked.

ashwin: Ugh. Is the regression only on FP8 or mixed precision too?

maria: Mostly when the runtime chooses the fp8_gemm path. Mixed precision (fp8 for matmul, fp16 acc) sometimes hits the faster kernel but selection seems shape-sensitive. Repro numbers below: 
```
# microbench (64 batch)
kernel=fp8_gemm shape=64x512 time=1.24ms
kernel=fp8_gemm shape=64x528 time=1.45ms
kernel=int8_gemm shape=64x512 time=1.05ms
kernel=int8_gemm shape=64x528 time=1.08ms
# baseline (no quant) fp16_gemm shape=64x512 time=1.02ms
```
Looks like when padding pushes width beyond a kernel-friendly boundary we fall into a much slower fp8 fallback.

kevin: Can you paste the kernel-selection log? I want to see the decision reason (shape, quant flag, runtime hint).

maria: snippet from logs: 
```
[select_kernel] model=llama-13b seq=512 padded_seq=528 tokens_ratio=0.117 quant=fp8 -> selected=fp8_generic_fallback (reason=shape_mismatch_to_fast_kernels)
[select_kernel] model=llama-13b seq=64 padded_seq=512 quant=int8 -> selected=int8_optimized_k128 (reason=shape_matches_tile)
```

yara: That tokens_ratio=0.117 shouldn't cause that huge perf cliff. I think there are two interacting issues: 1) our kernel shard table expects widths rounded to 32/64 boundaries, but fp8 optimized kernels only implemented for a subset of tile sizes; 2) continuous batching tends to merge different seq lengths and the padding pushes many groups over threshold causing fallback.

ashwin: Hypothesis: kernel-selection comparator uses a strict equality on tile-aligned width rather than the <=/nearest rule we intended. If so, a padded width of 528 (vs 512) will mismatch even though a slightly larger kernel would be fine.

kevin: Can you try forcing the selection to prefer int8 kernels when padded_ratio > 0.08 as a stopgap? That should reduce latency.

maria: Tried that locally — simple guard in runtime reduces p99 back to baseline: 
```
// pseudo-config
"kernel_selection": {
  "prefer_int8_if": "padded_tokens_ratio > 0.08 and batch_size >= 32"
}
```
Gives ~10-12% improvement in our continuous-batch scenario for the traffic shape.

yara: Long term we should: (A) extend fp8 optimized kernels to cover the common padded widths, or (B) change selection to pick nearest-fit kernel and let the kernel handle tail-handling instead of falling back. (A) is more work in kernels, (B) is a runtime change.

ashwin: Also worth checking KV cache impact — if KV cache chunking causes additional width inflation for decode steps we might see similar regressions for chat flows. Did you repro for incremental decode?

maria: Good call. For incremental decode the padding effect is even worse because kv cache alignment pads per-layer shapes. Profile excerpt: 
```
decode_step=1 padded_seq=16 kv_pad=8 effective_width=24 selected=fp8_generic_fallback time=0.42ms
decode_step=1 without_kv_pad selected=int8_opt time=0.28ms
```
So KV padding is multiplying the effect.

kevin: Ok actionable plan:
- maria: open a short PR to add the padded_ratio stopgap in selection config + perf test.
- ashwin/yara: investigate runtime selection comparator and nearest-fit logic.
- yara: file kernel backlog ticket to enumerate missing fp8 tile sizes.
- kevin: run a canary for a subset of traffic (canary id: fp8-pad-guard) after PR.

maria: Will open PR and attach bench harness + perf regression dashboard. Reference GH-3124 in PR.

devops-bot: deploy canary fp8-pad-guard to cluster r-4 with 1% traffic (triggered by kevin).

kevin: Thanks — priority high since this affects a lot of hosted customers. If we can't expand fp8 kernels quickly, guard + improved nearest-fit should be fine medium-term.

maria: filing PR now, will drop link when ready. :+1:
